## Where we are

::: {.incremental}
- Session 1: censoring, the Surv object, rates
- Today: **estimate and draw the survival curve** without assuming a constant rate
- By the end you can:
  - fit and read a **Kaplan-Meier** curve
  - report **survival at a time point** and the **median** (or "not reached")
  - draw curves by group with a **number-at-risk table**
:::

# Topic 1 — How the estimate is built {background-color="#2C3E50"}

## A step function

At each **event time**, survival drops by the fraction who die among those **still at risk**; **censored** patients leave the risk set without causing a drop.

::: {.eq}
S(t) = Π (1 − d~i~ / n~i~)  over event times ≤ t
:::

```{r}
toy <- tibble(time = c(2, 3, 3, 5, 7, 8), status = c(1, 1, 0, 1, 0, 1))
summary(survfit(Surv(time, status) ~ 1, toy))
```

## Reading the toy example

::: {.incremental}
- At time 2: 6 at risk, 1 dies: 1 × 5/6 = 0.83
- At time 3: 5 at risk, 1 dies and 1 is censored: 0.83 × 4/5 = 0.67
- The censored patient **counts in the denominator until censored**, then leaves
:::

## The overall curve

```{r}
km <- survfit(Surv(time_months, status) ~ 1, data = tb)
km
```

```{r}
#| output-location: slide
ggsurvfit(km) + add_confidence_interval() + labs(x = "Months since starting treatment", y = "Survival probability") + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0.5, 1))
```

# Topic 2 — Reading the curve {background-color="#2C3E50"}

## Survival at a time

```{r}
summary(km, times = c(6, 12, 18))
```

::: {.key}
"Survival at 12 months was **`r round(100 * summary(km, times = 12)$surv)`%** (95% CI `r round(100 * summary(km, times = 12)$lower)`–`r round(100 * summary(km, times = 12)$upper)`%)." Time points beyond the **longest follow-up** (here about 24 months) cannot be estimated.
:::

## The median survival time

::: {.incremental}
- The **median** is the time at which the curve **crosses 0.5**
- Here fewer than half the patients died, so the curve **never reaches 0.5**: the median is **not reached** (`NA`)
- Report **survival at fixed times** (12, 24 months) or the **restricted mean** instead
- Never replace "not reached" with the median of the observed times
:::

```{r}
summary(km)$table[c("records", "events", "median")]
```

## Confidence and the tail

::: {.warn}
The curve is **least reliable at the right end**, where **few patients remain at risk**: confidence bands widen and a single death moves the curve a lot. Always show the **number at risk** and avoid over-reading the tail.
:::

# Topic 3 — Curves by group {background-color="#2C3E50"}

## HIV-positive and negative

```{r}
km_grp <- survfit(Surv(time_months, status) ~ hiv, data = tb)
summary(km_grp, times = 12)$surv |> round(2)
```

```{r}
#| output-location: slide
ggsurvfit(km_grp) + add_confidence_interval() + add_risktable() + scale_ggsurvfit(x_scales = list(breaks = seq(0, 24, 6))) +
  labs(x = "Months since starting treatment", y = "Survival probability")
```

::: {.incremental}
- Positive patients have **lower survival** throughout
- **Overlapping bands** early on; separation grows
- The **risk table** shows how many remain: only **`r sum(tb$hiv == "Positive")`** HIV-positive patients started, so the right end is thin
:::

## Reporting a Kaplan-Meier analysis

::: {.good}
- **Number of patients and events** per group
- **Median follow-up** (reverse KM)
- **Survival at fixed times** with 95% CI, or the median with CI if reached
- The **figure** with number at risk, a clear axis and the **log-rank p-value** (Session 3)
:::

## Self-check quiz (1/5) {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_mcq("s2q1", "In a Kaplan-Meier analysis the median survival time is reported as 'not reached'. What does this mean?",
         c("The patients were followed for too short a time to be analysed",
           "The median could not be calculated because of missing data in the file",
           "Fewer than half of the patients had died by the end of follow-up",
           "More than half of the patients in the whole cohort were censored"), answer = 3,
         explain = "The median is where the curve crosses 0.5. If survival stays above 0.5 to the end of follow-up, the median is not reached; report survival at fixed times instead.")
```

## Self-check quiz (2/5) {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_mcq("s2q2", "What happens to a censored patient in the Kaplan-Meier calculation?",
         c("They are counted as a death at the time of censoring in the data",
           "They stay at risk until censored, then leave with no drop",
           "They are removed from the whole analysis from the very start of it",
           "They are counted as surviving until the end of the study period"), answer = 2,
         explain = "Censored patients count among those at risk up to their censoring time, then leave. They never cause a step down, but they shrink the denominator for later steps.")
```

## Self-check quiz (3/5) {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_mcq("s2q3", "Why should a Kaplan-Meier plot show the number at risk beneath the curve?",
         c("It gives the p-value for the comparison made between the two groups",
           "It shows the hazard ratio for each one of the groups in the plot",
           "The right end of the curve rests on few patients and is unreliable",
           "It is included only to make the plot look more complete and tidy"), answer = 3,
         explain = "The tail of the curve is estimated from the few patients still followed, so it is unstable. The risk table shows how much data support each part of the curve.")
```

## Self-check quiz (4/5) {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_mcq("s2q4", "At 12 months the Kaplan-Meier survival for HIV-positive patients is 0.72. How should this be stated?",
         c("72% of HIV-positive patients died within 12 months of starting treatment",
           "The hazard of dying in the HIV-positive group is 0.72 per month of time",
           "The median survival of HIV-positive patients is about 0.72 of a year",
           "About 72% of HIV-positive patients are estimated alive at 12 months"), answer = 4,
         explain = "S(12) is the probability of surviving beyond 12 months, so 72% survive to that point and 28% have died by then. It is not a hazard, a median, or the proportion who died.")
```

## Self-check quiz (5/5) {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_mcq("s2q5", "What is the survival estimate at 30 months if the longest follow-up in the data is 24 months?",
         c("It cannot be estimated from these data",
           "It is the same as the survival at 24 months",
           "It is zero, since nobody was followed that long",
           "It equals the median survival of the cohort"), answer = 1,
         explain = "Kaplan-Meier cannot extrapolate beyond the data. Reporting survival at times with no one at risk would be invention.")
```

## Score and take-home

**Your score: <span class="quiz-score"></span>**

::: {.incremental}
- KM estimates survival with a **step function**; censored patients **leave the risk set**
- Report **survival at fixed times** with CI; the **median** may be 'not reached'
- Always show the **number at risk**; beware the thin right tail
- KM is **descriptive**: the log-rank test and Cox model compare groups
:::
